past_actions.summary: Refresh LinkedIn profile to reflect full scope of HR expertise — workforce transition management, compliance, organizational development. Set profile to 'Open to Work' visible only to recruiters. Update resume with quantified outcomes: number of terminations managed, compliance programs implemented, cost-per-hire metrics. Target sectors: healthcare, tech, logistics, government — all growing headcount or facing their own restructuring needs.
past_actions.emotional_state: Calm and deliberate. The mild anxiety she carries (stress 0.29) is not panic — it's the productive discomfort of someone who sees clearly and hasn't yet acted on what she sees. She is not grieving this job or this industry. She is treating the situation like the project manager she secretly is: assess the landscape, reduce unnecessary exposure, activate the options that cost nothing to open. There is something almost relieving about finally moving from awareness to action.

past_actions.summary: Schedule a private consultation with an employment attorney — not the one she works with professionally on behalf of the company, but an independent one she identifies personally. Agenda: understand what a negotiated voluntary separation with severance looks like in her state, what triggers enhanced severance obligations, and whether her position as the person managing layoffs creates any particular legal standing or leverage. This is not whistleblowing and not adversarial — it is a competent professional learning her rights before she needs them.
past_actions.emotional_state: Angela is operating in what she privately thinks of as 'clear-eyed mode' — the emotional register she has observed in the best employees she has ever counseled through separations, the ones who arrived at her office already knowing what was coming and had already done most of their grieving before she said a word. There is something almost cold about it, but it is not coldness. It is the kind of clarity that comes from having seen this exact situation enough times to stop pretending it won't resolve the way it always resolves. Her stress has not spiked despite the announcement. If anything, confirmation is less stressful than suspicion. The dread of the unknown was worse than the known thing with a two-month timeline. She is not paralyzed. She is not manic. She is the most methodical she has been in years, which says something about how much energy she was spending pretending not to see what she saw.

past_actions.summary: Complete the car trade-down transaction this tick — not 'research,' not 'evaluate,' but execute. Walk into the dealership as a customer, not an employee-adjacent insider. Trade the current vehicle, take the equity, purchase a used vehicle outright using no more than $10,000 from savings — targeting something in the $8,000-10,000 range with low miles and low maintenance profile. Objective: eliminate the $649/month payment entirely. The net effect is an additional $649/month added to monthly margin, raising monthly surplus from approximately $589 to $1,238 — effectively doubling runway extension per month.
past_actions.emotional_state: Controlled and forward-facing. The grief — for the job, for the version of this career she thought she was building — was processed before this tick began. What's left is professional competence running alongside strategic self-interest, and she is no longer pretending those two things are in conflict. She is effective at her job because that effectiveness buys her time and leverage. She is building her exit because the exit is coming regardless of her feelings about it. These facts coexist without friction.
